PLACEMENT MOVED: FY2017 gave this its own page at the head of the Town Clerk section (p152); FY2018 appends it to the bottom of an election results page and the contents page does not list it at all. Deaths (96) are far above the 36 interments recorded by the cemetery department on p58 -- the two count different things and neither page says so.

tables.name: State primary results by precinct, September 4 2018
tables.what_it_is: Precinct-level results for the Democratic, Republican and Libertarian primary ballots, office by office, with blanks and write-ins.
tables.grain: one candidate (or BLANKS / Write-ins line) for one office on one party ballot
tables.layout: Six-column table with a party banner and an office heading over each block; offices confined to one House district show '---' in the precincts that did not vote on them
tables.printed_total: per-office TOTAL rows: Democratic 976, Republican 735, Libertarian 4
tables.notes: Extracts unusually cleanly for an election table -- one candidate per line with all five figures. FY2017 had only a badly OCR'd special primary; this is a full state primary and it is readable. Two mechanics matter: the House seats are split by precinct, so the 37th Middlesex block shows '---' for precinct B and totals 712 while the 3rd Worcester block shows '---' for A, C and D and totals 264 -- summing a column across offices will double-count or under-count unless the dashes are handled. And a footnote records a recount: '** Recount September 17, 2018 - No Change', with the two affected candidates marked '**' in the 3rd District congressional race. The Libertarian ballot (p243) had four voters town-wide and every row is blanks.

tables.name: State election results by precinct, November 6 2018
tables.what_it_is: Precinct-level results for every state and county office on the November 2018 ballot, plus the three statewide ballot questions.
tables.grain: one candidate or ballot-question response for one office
tables.layout: Six-column table; the ballot questions block puts the question number and short title in the left column and YES / NO / Blank as separate rows
tables.notes: Turnout 5,334 -- more than four times the town election. Column header capitalisation switches mid-table from 'PREC A' (p244) to 'Prec A' (p245 onward), and the totals row switches from 'Totals' to 'Total'. Ballot questions are labelled with short titles the town clerk supplied rather than official wording: 'Question #1 - Patient Safety' (nurse staffing ratios, NO 3680 to YES 1470), 'Question #2 - Citizen Commission', 'Question #3 - Anti-Discrimination'. The Register of Deeds race has only one candidate and 302 write-ins.

tables.name: Town and school employee gross wages, calendar 2018
tables.printed_heading: Town & School Employee Calendar 2018 Gross Wages
tables.what_it_is: Every person paid by the town or the schools in calendar year 2018, with surname, first name and gross wages.
tables.layout: Two side-by-side columns per page, seven pages, alphabetical by surname; the heading repeats on every page
tables.notes: THE DEPARTMENT COLUMN IS GONE. FY2017's version tagged every row with a paying department (SCHOOL, POLICE, FIRE, DPW, COA, LIBRARY, ACCT, TAX WORKOFF and a dozen more); FY2018 gives name and amount only. That removes the ability to split payroll by department, and it removes the only marker that identified senior tax work-off participants. It also means the two years cannot be joined on department. Offsetting that, this year's extraction is cleaner -- FY2017's OCR dropped some surnames entirely and mangled amounts; FY2018's is a layout-mode text layer with the pipe separators intact. Still no printed total in either year, and still a CALENDAR year against the report's FISCAL year figures, so it will not tie to the payroll lines in the appropriations table. Two rows read 'BRODEN | JAMES' with different amounts ($1,500.00 and $6,569.70) -- either two people or one person paid from two sources, and nothing on the page distinguishes them.

tables.name: Board and committee meeting schedule
tables.what_it_is: When and where each board, commission and committee regularly meets.
tables.layout: Four-column list on a single page
tables.notes: SHORTER THAN FY2017: 15 bodies against 22, and it now fits on one page where FY2017 needed two. Dropped entirely: Board of Assessors, Capital Planning Committee, Cemetery Commission, Green Community Task Force, Parks Commission, Personnel Committee. Whether those bodies stopped meeting or were simply omitted is not stated -- the page adds a caveat FY2017 did not have: 'Please check the Town website or with the Town Clerk office ... and for other committee or board meeting times and locations', which implies omission rather than dissolution. Board of Health moved from Tuesdays to Mondays; Public Access Cable from 2nd to 1st Monday; the Sewer Commission row has lost its DAY value.

tables.name: Town office hours and phone numbers
tables.what_it_is: Each town office with its opening hours and telephone number.
tables.layout: Three-column list; hours often wrap to a second line
tables.notes: Still states 'ALL TOWN OFFICES, EXCEPT WHERE NOTED, ARE CLOSED ON FRIDAYS.' New entry: HUMAN RESOURCES with its own hours and number -- a department that did not appear in FY2017. GONE: the WATER DISTRICT OFFICE row, which in FY2017 carried the footnote explaining that the Water District 'is a separate distinct municipal entity not associated with the Town of Lunenburg'; that clarification is no longer printed anywhere. The Teen Center entry is renamed 'CHESTER MOSSMAN TEEN CENTER / BOYS & GIRLS CLUB OF LUNENBURG' and its phone number changed. Several accounting and assessing numbers now list two extensions.

surprises: The entire Monty Tech FINANCIAL section is missing. FY2017 carried eight Monty Tech tables at pp140-149 -- balance sheet, budget summary, five-year income and expense, expenditures by DESE function code, DESE's Chapter 70 worksheet, foundation enrollment vs school attending children, assessment ratio percentages, community assessments, and a twenty-year assessment history. FY2018's Monty Tech section stops at p149 with the school committee roster and contains NONE of them. Lunenburg's Monty Tech assessment appears in FY2018 only as a single omnibus budget line. A search for 'COMMUNITY ASSESSMENTS' or 'ASSESSMENT HISTORY' returns nothing in this document.

The FY2018 report silently corrects a digit-drop in the FY2017 report. FY2017 printed 2017 Bond Anticipation Notes as $295,925 and total outstanding indebtedness as $52,093,784; FY2018's five-year debt table prints the same year as $2,895,925 and $54,693,785 -- and FY2017's own balance sheet said BANS PAYABLE $2,895,925.00. Neither report flags the correction.

The FY2019 omnibus budget table foots to $36,804,408.83 under a heading and an article vote that both say $36,867,903.83, and the Town Manager's report gives a third figure, $36,813,954.63, for the same budget. All three are in this one document.

Monty Tech's per-program gender split vanished. FY2017 gave male/female counts for all twenty vocational programs in parentheticals; FY2018 gives only a total, while the narrative on the same page still asserts the student body is 'well-balanced by gender'.

The employee wage table lost its department column between the two years, so calendar 2018 payroll cannot be split by department at all -- and the senior property-tax work-off participants, who were identifiable in FY2017 by a 'TAX WORKOFF' tag, are now indistinguishable from ordinary employees.

The cemetery report prints an explicit correction to the previous year's town report ('Note: Correction on 2017 Town Report- *Lillian Griffiths Age: 99 North') -- the FY2017 report had printed her surname as Griffin. It also starts printing a total (18 full burials, 18 cremations, 36 total) where FY2017 printed none.

Two structured datasets exist only as prose or charts: the Finance Committee's department-by-department FY2019 budget changes are a bulleted list (p69-70), and Monty Tech's per-town enrollment survives only as bar-chart data labels whose pairing with town names has to be inferred from position (p137).
The town profile page says 7,870 registered voters; the May 2018 election tally sheet on p234 says 7,799. Both are in the same report and neither reconciles to the other.

The vital records counts moved off their own page and were appended to the bottom of an election tally page (p236), and the contents page does not list them -- so a heading- or contents-driven search for vital records in FY2018 finds nothing.

Article 7 of the November Special Town Meeting reprints an entire bylaw section with additions underlined and deletions struck through, but the strike-through markup does not survive text extraction, so the extracted text runs the old and new wording together ('payable on the last first payroll warrant in Julyne') and the paid-vacation table's first row collides into a nonexistent '808 hours'.
